title: Mujaddara
subtitle: Middle Eastern rice and lentils with crispy onions
excerpt: A simple dish of rice and green lentils topped with deeply caramelised onions. It is filling, cheap, and much greater than its ingredients suggest.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from Levantine home cooking traditions. The crispy onion topping is the defining element across all regional versions.

content.text: Take your time with the onions. They need to go dark and crispy, not just soft and golden.

items.prepNote: 2 thinly sliced for the crispy topping, 1 finely diced for the base

content.text: Put the lentils in a large saucepan. Cover with plenty of cold water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until just tender. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, heat 4 tablespoons of oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the 2 thinly sliced onions with a pinch of salt.
Cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the onions are deep brown and crispy. Remove and spread on a plate lined with kitchen paper.
In the same saucepan used for the lentils, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. Fry the diced onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cumin, cinnamon, and allspice. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rinsed rice and the drained lentils. Stir to coat. Pour in 500ml of water and add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil. Cover tightly and reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Squeeze over the lemon juice and toss. Spoon onto plates, pile on the crispy onions, and scatter mint on top. Serve with yoghurt on the side.

items.symptom: Rice is undercooked in the centre.
items.fix: Keep the lid on; do not lift it for the full 15 minutes.

items.symptom: Onions are soft and pale, not crispy.
items.cause: Too much oil or heat too low.
items.fix: Use medium-high heat and spread onions thinly in the pan.

items.cause: Not enough salt in the cooking water.
items.fix: Season the water generously before adding rice and lentils.
